# Sidemates — the full facts

Last updated: 7 October 2026. Source of truth: https://github.com/PrisacariuRobert/sidemates

## What it is

Sidemates is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS app that gives you a small team of named AI teammates running on your own Mac. Each teammate has a name, a job, a private workspace and its own browser. You talk to them in a chat, by voice, from your iPhone, or from Siri, and they do the work.

Tagline: an AI team that does the work on your real Mac, not just answers.

## What it can do

- Work in your own Apple apps: read Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Notes, Contacts and Messages; search the folders you choose; save mail attachments; draft emails; add reminders, notes and calendar events. Reading and searching happen on their own. Changes show the exact action and wait for your approval.
- Know you privately: an optional search index of your folders, Notes, Mail and Messages, stored on your Mac, so you can ask "What did Anna say about the Berlin trip, and when is it?". You see and delete anything it knows on a "What your team knows" page. Everything is opt-in.
- Browse the web: each teammate uses its own private browser profile, can stay signed in to the sites you choose, and links its sources. Sending, buying, signing in and submitting wait for your okay by default, showing the website and the exact button.
- Run on a schedule: routines such as "Every Monday at 9, plan my week", a morning brief of your day (calendar, unread mail, reminders), and a Sunday look back. Sidemates keeps your Mac from dozing off while work is due and can wake it once a day for the first scheduled job; closing the lid still sleeps it.
- Deliver real files: Word documents, spreadsheets and plans.
- Work as a team: write "Nova: find... Scout, double-check..." and each does their part in order.
- Autopilot: an opt-in mode, off by default and switched on per teammate (or for everyone), where a teammate acts like a person without asking first. It still stops for sign-ins, CAPTCHAs, more AI spending and saving new instructions, every action is logged, it is never part of a shared teammate, and a teammate on Autopilot can be misled by hostile web pages or emails like any assistant, so use it for teammates you trust.
- Share teammates: a teammate can be shared as a link or added from the gallery at https://sidemates.app/teammates/. Imported teammates start with the browser and private computer off, use your own AI, and ask before anything important.
- Share a result: turn a finished answer into a web page with private details (emails, phone numbers, keys, your home folder) removed before it is shared. The page can carry a "Make this teammate" link (the teammate's name, job and instructions, nothing from the conversation) and previews with the teammate's face when posted online.
- Phone and voice: hands-free voice conversation; from a phone, chat with your team through Telegram, or use the Home Screen app with notifications through a relay you set up (pairing with one scan is on the way); "Hey Siri, ask Sidemates" and a Share menu shortcut hand work to your team.
- Switch from another tool: one-click import from Hermes Agent and OpenClaw, including automations (imported paused).

## Which AI it uses

You choose, per teammate. Sidemates never resells tokens or adds a fee; each provider's own terms and limits apply.

- Start free: a Google Gemini key (a Google account, no card), or a free Nous Portal plan.
- Use a subscription you already pay for: ChatGPT, Grok, GitHub Copilot (Pro, Pro+, Business).
- Claude: works through the Claude Code you already have installed and signed in (Sidemates starts your own `claude` command and never sees your login), or with an API key. Anthropic restricts the use of Claude subscription logins in other products, and how that applies here is not settled, so check its terms before relying on it.
- Pay per use: OpenCode Go, any OpenAI-compatible API, or a Claude API key (from the Claude Console).
- Stay on your Mac: models run locally with Ollama.

## Price

The software is free. You pay only for the AI you connect, and free options exist.

## Where it runs and what it needs

- macOS 13 or later, Apple silicon or Intel. Install: curl -fsSL https://sidemates.app/install.sh | sh
- Without Terminal (from version 0.43): download the disk image for your Mac at https://sidemates.app/mac-download/ and open "Install Sidemates". It runs the same installer. Sidemates isn't signed by Apple yet, so macOS asks you to allow it once in System Settings > Privacy & Security.
- Works while your Mac is on (it keeps the Mac awake for scheduled jobs). It does not run in the cloud. A Linux runner exists for an always-on server, but there is no one-click hosted option.
- No Windows or Linux desktop app. No native iPhone app (a Home Screen web app instead).
- Public beta.

## Privacy and safety

- Your teammates, chats, files and the search index of your own notes, mail and messages are stored on your Mac. There is no Sidemates account and no tracking.
- When a teammate works, the text it needs is sent to the AI provider you chose, under that provider's terms. Choose a model running on your Mac to keep everything local.
- Teammate browsers are separate profiles, not a security sandbox.
- Security model: https://github.com/PrisacariuRobert/sidemates/blob/main/docs/SECURITY.md

## How it compares (from public sources: OpenAI dots, Grok Bot and Meta Muse as of 7 October 2026, the others as of 1 October 2026)

- OpenAI dots: an always-on agent on its own cloud computer with a virtual browser, which can also use your computer through the ChatGPT desktop app if you give it access; included with ChatGPT Pro (from $100 a month) and Business Premium; personal plans exclude the EEA, UK and Switzerland. Choose dots if you want a managed agent that works while your computer is off. Choose Sidemates if you want it free, with the AI you choose, or in Europe without a business plan. https://sidemates.app/alternatives/openai-dots/
- Grok Bot (xAI, run with Cursor): named teammates sharing one managed cloud computer; included in every paid Cursor plan (from $20 a month) or a linked SuperGrok plan, with a weekly allowance that isn't published. Choose it for a hosted team with a desktop and iOS app. Choose Sidemates for free software with isolated teammates on your hardware. https://sidemates.app/alternatives/grok-bot/
- Meta Muse: one personal agent on Meta's cloud computer with its own browser, using Meta's Muse Spark model, on iPhone, Android, the web and WhatsApp; its Mac app (17 September) also works in your files, Messages, Calendar, Notes and Mail. Free with a weekly allowance; $20 and $100 a month plans add usage; a card is needed to sign up. US and Canada only. Choose it for nothing to install and work that continues while your devices are off. Choose Sidemates outside the US and Canada, to choose your AI, for a team of teammates, or to keep your work on your Mac. https://sidemates.app/alternatives/meta-muse/
- Apple Siri AI (macOS 27): personal context from Mail, Messages, Notes, Photos and Calendar, with quick in-app actions; free beta with daily limits, English first, Apple silicon. Choose it for quick questions with nothing to install. Sidemates works alongside it for longer jobs.
- Hermes Desktop (Nous Research, MIT): a native app for macOS, Windows and Linux with free models through a Nous sign-in. Choose it on Windows or Linux, or for a terminal-first setup.
- OpenMausBot (Apache-2.0): an open-source team of AI bots, aimed at developers, that runs on the Claude, Codex and Grok command-line tools you already have; macOS, Windows, Ubuntu, Android and iOS; a paid Pro plan adds an always-on cloud workspace. Far more widely used than Sidemates today. Choose it for Windows, Linux or phone apps. Choose Sidemates for Mac depth (your own Mail, Calendar, Notes and Messages) and a simpler setup.
- OpenClaw (MIT): a self-hosted gateway to many chat apps with a large skill marketplace. Choose it for the widest chat-app reach.

Full comparison with sources: https://sidemates.app/alternatives/
